title: Automated diagnostic bundles + per-tenant retry hysteresis to reduce 5xx cascades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
In the last three production escalations we observed correlated 5xx waves driven by aggressive client retries and opaque failure context. On-call runs frequently require manual data collection (spans, tenant traces, socket states) and ad-hoc temporary retry reductions. This increases MTTR and leads to customer-visible retries and billing surprises.

Problem statement:
- We lack an automated, per-tenant diagnostic bundle that is triggered early in escalations and contains all artifacts engineers need to triage (request traces, proxy metrics, kernel evictions, KV cache stats, connection pools).
- Global retry policies are too coarse: tenants experiencing transient backend saturation continue to receive retry amplification for the full circuit-breaker window, causing prolonged 5xx cascades.

Goals:
1) Implement an automated escalation-triggered diagnostic bundle generator that collects a standardized set of artifacts and uploads to a secure bucket with short TTL, linked in the incident.
2) Implement a per-tenant "retry hysteresis" window: when a tenant shows sustained 5xx > threshold, temporarily reduce client-facing recommended retry behavior (grace period) and apply gentler backoff/hard limits to prevent amplification.
3) Expose telemetry and dashboards so PMs/SEs can see both bundle attachments and the state of per-tenant hysteresis in near-real time.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change default SDK retry semantics shipped to customers (that requires separate SDK release).
- Not addressing deep kernel scheduling tuning; scope limited to orchestration, policy, and observability.

Proposed solution (high level):
1) Diagnostic bundles
  - New service side endpoint (diagnostics collector) that pulls: trace spans (request-level), nginx/proxy connection stats, GPU/KV cache eviction logs, model runtime error counts, tenant token usage snapshot, recent client retry headers.
  - Trigger: bundle auto-generated when tenant 5xx rate > 7% for 1m AND error rate trend is increasing for 2 consecutive 30s windows OR when an incident escalation flag is set by oncall.
  - Bundles stored in S3 with name pattern: redwood-diag/{tenant}/{timestamp}/{incident-id}.zip, TTL 7 days, access via signed URL included in incident channel.

2) Per-tenant retry hysteresis
  - Policy engine change: add state for tenant = {Healthy | Hysteresis}, with Hysteresis entered when 5xx% > 7% for 90s; exit after 10 minutes of 5xx% < 2% or manual clear by oncall.
  - While in Hysteresis: override downstream recommended retry header to client: Retry-After: jittered exponential starting at 800ms with max attempts 2. Also apply server-side request shaping: drop traffic beyond soft qps cap to preserve stability and return 429 instead of 500 where reasonable.
  - Make policy configurable per tenant via console (post-implementation follow-up ticket).

3) Observability & Runbook
  - New dashboard panels: per-tenant 5xx%, hysteresis-state, bundle generation events, average retry count per request.
  - Update runbook with steps: how to fetch bundle, how to clear hysteresis state, rollback plan, and customer communication templates.

Acceptance criteria:
- Automated bundles created for simulated tenant failure in staging and uploaded to S3 with correct artifacts present.
- Hysteresis policy prevents retry amplification in a synthetic test where client retries are aggressive (reduce per-request retries by >= 60% and limit peak 5xx contagion).
- Dashboard shows hysteresis state and bundle events for test tenant.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch + integration tests against a local bundle collector stub and fake S3 (2 days).
2) Canary deploy of diagnostic collector + policy flag disabled by default (1 day).
3) Enable hysteresis in canary region for internal tenants and run chaos scenarios (3 days).
4) Gradual enablement for small external tenants with customer notifications; monitor for false positives (7 days).

Risks and mitigations:
- False positive hysteresis could throttle healthy tenants: start with conservative thresholds and provide manual clear path.
- Bundles may contain sensitive data: ensure automatic scrubbing of PII and restrict signed URL TTL to 7 days.

Longer-term follow-ups:
- Console UI for tenant-level hysteresis tuning and audit logs (separate PM ticket).
- SDK opt-in hints so clients can adapt to server-provided Retry-After semantics.
